quick_skim.title: It Takes Two to Match: Co-Evolving Generative Retriever with Reinforcement Learning
quick_skim.abstract: Retrieval is the first stage of modern search and advertising systems, selecting a candidate set from a large item universe for downstream ranking and auction. Recent work increasingly leverages LLMs to improve retrieval through query expansion, data synthesis, and retrieval-feedback training. However, the generative component is typically used for query-side augmentation, while final matching is still delegated to a downstream retriever. We introduce CoGR, a retrieval framework that instead trains LLMs to directly construct retrieval representations on both query and item sides. Each generator produces a compact set of keywords, which are matched directly through an inverted index, preserving compatibility with existing keyword-based retrieval infrastructure. CoGR uses a two-stage training pipeline. Supervised fine-tuning first establishes an aligned keyword space, after which co-evolving reinforcement learning alternately optimizes the query- and item-side generators with GRPO against the opposite side's frozen index. Both sides optimize the same query-to-item retrieval $F_1$ objective: the query side receives retrieval $F_1$ directly, while the item side receives a counterfactual marginal reward measuring the change in query-side $F_1$ caused by its generated keywords. Across 10 representative sparse, dense, and generative baselines, CoGR achieves the best performance on both an internal APP Marketplace dataset and the public WANDS benchmark, improving $F_1$ over the strongest baseline by $10.9\%$ and $36.1\%$, respectively. Further analysis shows stable co-evolution and increasingly aligned query--item keyword spaces over training.

quick_skim.llm_tldr_en: Presents CoGR, an RL-trained retrieval framework where LLMs directly construct compact query and item keyword representations, creating an inverted-index matcher rather than using query-side augmentation only. Experimental results demonstrate effective co-evolution of both sides for retrieval.
quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 现有生成式检索多利用语言模型做查询扩展，最终仍由下游检索器匹配，两端表示难以协同。CoGR框架使用强化学习训练查询端和文档端的生成器，直接构造紧凑关键词表示，并靠倒排索引完成匹配。实验证明这种协同演进的表示生成可有效改善检索性能，同时保持与传统关键词检索的兼容性。该工作展示了强化学习在检索表示构造上的潜力。
